title: Billing Basis of the Keyturn Vehicle Care Plan: Monthly Fee, Chargeable Work and Reimbursement
content:
The monthly fee for a Keyturn Vehicle Care Plan is billed on the plan's billing day, and where that day does not exist in a short month the fee is billed on the last day of that month instead.

### Charges on work

Work outside the allowance is invoiced at the plan's discounted parts rate with labour capped at the plan's hourly ceiling, and a workshop charging above the cap is paid the cap while the host pays nothing more.

The host pays the plan's per-visit excess where the plan carries one, and the excess is charged once per visit however many jobs the visit covers.

Nothing more is met once the plan's spend ceiling for the term has been reached, and the host is told what has been spent rather than discovering it at the next invoice.

### Work done outside the network

Work at a workshop outside the network is reimbursed at the plan's out-of-network share of the invoice, capped at the plan's out-of-network ceiling, and only on the plans that reimburse at all.

The amount reimbursed for one such visit is the lower of two quantities: the invoiced amount multiplied by the plan's out-of-network share and rounded to the nearest cent, and the plan's out-of-network ceiling. The share acts on the whole of the invoiced amount, and the ceiling is applied to the result of that multiplication rather than to the invoice.

*Worked illustration on hypothetical figures.* Take an invoice of USD 333.33 for work done outside the network, on a plan whose out-of-network share is 60 percent and whose ceiling on one visit is USD 200.00. Sixty percent of 333.33 is 199.998, which rounded to the nearest cent is 200.00. That figure is not above the ceiling of 200.00, so 200.00 is reimbursed. On an invoice of USD 400.00 under the same hypothetical terms, sixty percent is 240.00, which stands above the ceiling, so 200.00 is reimbursed. These figures are hypothetical; each plan sets its own share and its own ceiling.

### Disputes and the warranty on work

An invoice may be disputed inside the plan's dispute period, counted in whole calendar days from the day the invoice was raised, and work is guaranteed for the plan's warranty period, within which the same fault is put right at no charge.

The dispute period is read against the marketplace's own record of the invoice and of the visit it belongs to, and against the day that record shows the invoice was raised, rather than against the day the host says they opened it. The period is counted in whole calendar days from that day, and the day on which it runs out is itself still inside it.

*On both sides of that boundary.* An invoice raised on a given day, on a plan whose dispute period is a number of calendar days, may be disputed up to and including the day that falls that many calendar days after the day it was raised. On the following day the period has run and the invoice may no longer be disputed.
